title: Basic sewing
examples: What kind of thread should I use for jeans?
Is it okay if my stitches are not perfectly straight?
Can I use a machine if I am learning to sew by hand?

explain.say: First we learn how to thread a needle safely.

items: 1. Thread the end through the eye.
2. Pull the thread through the eye.

explain.say: Next we practice the running stitch for straight lines.

items: 1. Push the needle through the fabric.
2. Pull the thread back through the fabric.

explain.say: A running stitch makes small, even, straight lines.
To sew a button we first need to create a hole.

items: 2. Use a tool to poke the hole.

explain.say: Then we use the running stitch to secure the button.
In real life you sew a button on a jacket.

faq.q: Do I need to tie a knot at the end of the thread?
faq.a: Yes, you should always tie a secure knot at the very end of your thread. This keeps the stitching from coming undone later.
asks: How do I finish my thread?
What do I do when I finish sewing?

faq.q: What is the best type of thread to use?
faq.a: For beginners, a strong, plain cotton thread works very well. You can choose a color that matches your fabric for best results.
asks: Should the thread be thick or thin?

faq.q: How far apart should my running stitches be?
faq.a: Try to keep your running stitches about the width of a pencil eraser apart. This gives the fabric enough room to breathe.
asks: What is the right spacing for stitches?
Are my stitches too close together?

faq.q: Do I have to use a special tool to make the button hole?
faq.a: A sturdy needle or a small awl tool can help you poke a neat hole. Always ask an adult before poking holes in clothes.
asks: Is it hard to make a hole?

faq.q: If I sew too tightly, what happens?
faq.a: If you sew too tightly, the fabric around the button might get too strained. This could make the seam look bumpy or stressed.
asks: What is the problem with tight sewing?
Should I pull hard when sewing?

facts: A running stitch is a basic hand sewing technique.
You must thread the needle before you can sew.
Sewing a button requires creating a hole first.
A knot is used to secure the end of the thread.

quiz.say: When threading the needle, what is the first step?

options.show: Use a pin to push the thread.
options.say: Use a pin to push the thread.

options.show: Pass the end of the thread through the eye.
options.say: Pass the end of the thread through the eye.

options.show: Tie a knot around the needle.
options.say: Tie a knot around the needle.

options.show: Push the thread through the fabric.
options.say: Push the thread through the fabric.

quiz.why: You must pass the thread through the eye first to begin the process.

wrong.0: Pins are for holding fabric, not for passing thread through the eye.
wrong.2: You cannot tie a knot around the needle; the thread goes through the eye.
wrong.3: You are learning to thread the needle first, not sewing it to fabric.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of the running stitch?

options.show: To create a straight, visible line of stitching.
options.say: To create a straight, visible line of stitching.

options.show: To strengthen the whole piece of cloth.
options.say: To strengthen the whole piece of cloth.

options.show: To hold the button in place alone.
options.say: To hold the button in place alone.

quiz.why: The running stitch creates a simple, continuous line when you pull the thread through.

wrong.1: The running stitch is visible and is used for joining or decorating.
wrong.2: While it strengthens, its primary role is creating a line, not overall structure.
wrong.3: You must first make a hole before the stitch can hold the button.

quiz.say: When sewing a button, what must happen before stitching?

options.show: Tie the thread directly around the button.
options.say: Tie the thread directly around the button.

options.show: Just push the button through the fabric.
options.say: Just push the button through the fabric.

options.show: Use glue to stick the button on.
options.say: Use glue to stick the button on.

options.show: A hole must be carefully poked through the fabric.
options.say: A hole must be carefully poked through the fabric.

quiz.why: You cannot sew a button onto fabric without first making a hole for it to pass through.

wrong.0: Tying it directly will not let the button sit flat and secure.
wrong.1: The button needs a hole to pass through smoothly, it cannot just be pushed.
wrong.2: Glue is not a sewing method, and the stitch is needed for a strong fix.
